answer: Quorum disagreement triggers a second panel, a rule requiring an independent reviewer set whenever signer subsets diverge. Each signer must lock a ridge of stake that the panel slashes upon finding collusion, and only the panel may penalise. A thousand fakes cost a thousand stakes, because bonding scales with identity count, not with cheap key generation. Honest clusters show a prism of consistent attestations, while farms fracture into divergent quills of contradictory votes. Attack cost scales linearly, forcing forged identities to burn capital faster than they can recruit.
